Hazardous situation: ECG R-peak missed in a degraded or atypical waveform
Potential harm: Incorrect heart rate or missed event if used clinically
Proposed controls: Abstain on invalid signal and do not present as diagnosis; independent clinical validation
Verification evidence: Full-dataset per-record FN and hazard-specific tests

Hazardous situation: Extra peaks due to artifacts or T-waves
Potential harm: False clinical event or alarm burden if used clinically
Proposed controls: Signal quality gate with independent review and explicit uncertainty

Hazardous situation: Lead naming or sampling-rate mapping wrong
Proposed controls: Check original metadata and compare against WFDB references

Hazardous situation: Dataset leakage or benchmark tuning invalidates metrics
Potential harm: Misleading evidence and unsafe deployment decisions
Proposed controls: Fixed protocol; code hashes; separate development and independent test sets

Hazardous situation: Quality index mistaken for clinical probability
Proposed controls: Research-only labels and task-specific calibration study
Verification evidence: Human factors review and calibration study

Hazardous situation: Processing errors silently omitted
Proposed controls: Fail incomplete evaluations; retain per-record errors

Hazardous situation: Patient-identifiable data stored or exported unprotected
Proposed controls: Strict research data policy; clinical-grade access control encryption and retention design
Verification evidence: Independent threat model and security tests

Hazardous situation: Unapproved integration impacts live patient alarm
Potential harm: Delayed response to critical physiological event
Proposed controls: Block live alarm routing and patient-affecting actions until authorized
Verification evidence: Architecture inspection and integration negative tests

Hazardous situation: Wrong reviewer label or annotation timing
Potential harm: Training contamination or misleading reference metrics
Proposed controls: Reviewer provenance

Hazardous situation: Software update changes model behavior
Proposed controls: Locked version and dependency manifests; automated regression and post-deployment monitoring
Verification evidence: Controlled change review and validated release tests

Hazardous situation: Legacy archives lacking verified artifact digest
Proposed controls: Mark old cases unverified and require review

Hazardous situation: Stored waveform archive altered after import
Proposed controls: Check saved artifact SHA-256 and fail closed on mismatch

Hazardous situation: Malformed archive overwhelms parser
Proposed controls: Restrict NPZ declared size and keys; security fuzzing

Hazardous situation: Spreadsheet interprets exported record text as formula
Potential harm: Execution of untrusted formula in exported artifact
Proposed controls: Escape formula-like text; downstream consumer tests

Hazardous situation: Unauthenticated access to local workspaces
Proposed controls: No patient data permitted; design SSO RBAC encryption and authorization

Hazardous situation: Weak or lost local encryption passphrase
Potential harm: Research export disclosure or irreversible loss of research data
Proposed controls: Long passphrase and authenticated AES-GCM; safe recovery procedure and institutional backups needed
Verification evidence: Security negative tests and offsite key recovery design

Hazardous situation: Audit and HMAC key modified together by privileged actor
Potential harm: False trust in research audit history
Proposed controls: Keep authenticated anchor and key outside workspace with independent custodian
Verification evidence: External anchor tampering/truncation tests and future SIEM deployment

Hazardous situation: CSV import causes memory exhaustion
Potential harm: Application crash and incomplete research analysis
Proposed controls: Maximum input size and cell limit; benchmark with realistic upper bounds

Hazardous situation: Research export ZIP or CSV read as protected patient-data storage
Proposed controls: Explicit unencrypted-export warning; protected path design needed
Verification evidence: Human factors testing for export dialogs

Hazardous situation: Self-generated engineering test report mistaken for regulatory authorization
Proposed controls: Hard clinical release gate and unambiguous evidence limitations
Verification evidence: Fail-closed gate tests; formal independent review
